newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANUCKS BEAT SABRES 7-6 IN OVERTIME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANUCKS BEAT SABRES 7-6 IN OVERTIME.

text.p: Mike Sillinger beat Dominik Hasek with 82 seconds to play in overtime as the Vancouver Canucks defeated the Buffalo Sabres 7-6 Wednesday in a wild game that saw a see-saw six-goal third period.

With just under 1:30 left in the extra period, Esa Tikkanen broke into the left faceoff circle but lost the puck off his stick. It trickled just outside the circle where Sillinger was able to spin and get a shot off.
The puck bounced past a Buffalo defender and through Hasek's pads for the game-winner.
"Just a funny game, lots of goals back and forth, an exciting game for the fans to watch, a coach's nightmare," Sillinger said.
Buffalo's Michal Grosek recorded his first career hat trick. He entered with just four goals in 25 games this season, but scored twice in the third, including the tying tally with 2:43 left.

The Sabres had their three-game winning streak snapped and surrendered seven goals after allowing only 11 in their previous six contests. They failed to outshoot an opponent for the 26th time in as many games this season.
"They got some lucky bounces," Sabres centre Mike Peca said. "I thought when we put it to 6-5 we had them going. It's just a matter of us getting the tying goal.

"We came back in overtime and outchanced them, but they came back and got the goal. You can look at it two ways -- we didn't deserve it from the start or we battled back and deserved to win, but we didn't."

Making Vancouver's offensive outburst even more surprising was that the Canucks did it without offensive stars Trevor Linden, Alexander Mogilny and Russ Courtnall, out with injuries. The Canucks had 38 shots after totalling only 34 in their previous two games.

At Colorado, Patrick Roy made 36 saves, including a series of dazzling stops in the third period, to record his league-leading fifth shutout of the season as the Avalanche blanked the Edmonton Oilers, 2-0.

Joe Sakic scored a shorthanded goal with 6:21 left in the second period and Peter Forsberg scored an empty-net goal and set up the other for the Avalanche, who have won four of their last five and are unbeaten in 10 of their last 11 at home.

Roy, who leads all active goalies with 35 career shutouts, turned aside 20 shots in the third period alone. He broke up a 2-on-none break with 14:14 remaining, then made four consecutive stops after Edmonton lifted goalie Curtis Joseph for an extra attacker in the final minute.
In New York, Eric Lindros scored his first goal of the season with 6:35 to go, lifting the Philadelphia Flyers into a 1-1 tie with the Rangers in an Atlantic Division battle.

Dale Hawerchuk won a faceoff deep in the Rangers' zone and fed the puck back to Lindros, who fired a slap shot from the top of the left circle that beat goaltender Mike Richter low to the glove side. Lindros missed the first 23 games of the season with a groin injury.
Richter, a Philadelphia-area native, turned aside 39 shots and Brian Noonan had the only goal for the Rangers, unbeaten in their last four games (3-0-1).
In Ottawa, Jaromir Jagr scored his league-leading 24th goal to cap a three-goal second period and lift the Pittsburgh Penguins to 4-2 victory over the Senators.
With the game tied 2-2, Jagr beat Ottawa goaltender Damian Rhodes to give the Penguins their first lead.
Stu Barnes and Andreas Johansson also scored in a 4:34 span for Pittsburgh, which had three goals on just six shots in the second period. Ron Francis added a third-period goal.
At Washington, Kevin Hodson made 19 saves for his second career shutout and Darren McCarty and Sergei Fedorov scored to lead the Detroit Red Wings to a 2-0 blanking of the Capitals.
Hodson, appearing in his sixth NHL game and making his second start of the season, got his first shutout of the season and Detroit's fourth.

In Anaheim, Teemu Selanne scored with 4:17 left in the third period to snap a tie and added an empty-net goal and Guy Hebert made 37 saves as the Mighty Ducks handed the reeling Tampa Bay Lightning their sixth straight loss, 3-1.
Steve Rucchin added a goal and two assists for the Ducks, who have won five of their last six games. Hebert has allowed just seven goals in that span.
In Montreal, Rob DiMaio scored off his own rebound with 4:11 remaining and the Boston Bruins held on for a 4-3 victory over the Canadiens.
The Bruins squandered a three-goal lead, but DiMaio tallied for the third time in as many games to help Boston to its third win in four contests.
Jozef Stumpel had a goal and an assist for the Bruins.

In Dallas, Kelly Hrudey stopped 35 shots and Ulf Dahlen and Marty McSorley scored as the San Jose Sharks edged the Stars 2-1 to post consecutive wins for the first time in five weeks. The win was just San Jose's third in its last 13 games.
